learning: Only LLM proposals can create procedures; admission requires all prior independently signed observations and production procedural consolidation. Every episode updates support and calibration.
tools: All arms have the same bounded affine interpreter; only admitted learned procedures supply coefficients. No oracle or symbolic rule fitter is available to the agent.
forecast: Before arithmetic execution, immutable production forecasts use evidence support with Laplace risk and a union bound; signed separate-process oracle outcomes resolve them.
analysis: Same six simultaneous bounds and success thresholds as v1; scores concern tool-assisted agent output. Raw LLM responses are retained separately.
stopping: One fresh sealed corpus; no tuning or retries after observed outcomes.
limitations: Bounded affine-domain agent, not a qualification of the complete autonomous GenOS runtime or general competence.
LLM weights remain fixed; learning is external verified procedural memory and evidence-driven confidence.
The interpreter is an explicit additional tool compared with historical v1; v1 and v2 scores are not a matched causal comparison.
The local oracle and signer share the experimenter's trust boundary; not an independent laboratory.
The support-based probability is a conservative operational forecast whose calibration is measured, not assumed.
